news.headline: uniQure submits biologics license application to FDA for ifezuntirgene inilparvo
uniQure submits BLA to FDA and MAA to MHRA for AMT-130 in Huntington’s disease
uniQure Announces Submission of Biologics License
ICER opens a cost-effectiveness review of uniQure's AMT-130 with a March 2027 public meeting
news.summary: The Institute for Clinical and Economic Review launched an assessment of AMT-130 (nonproprietary name ifezuntrigene inilparvovec) for Huntington's disease, with a scoping comment period running August 20 to September 11, 2026. A draft evidence report is due January 19, 2027, a Midwest CEPAC public meeting is set for March 25, 2027 and the final report for April 29, 2027 - the first formal US payer-value review of the therapy and an early marker for the pricing debate.

news.headline: RTW Investments and Susquehanna disclose new stakes in uniQure in 13G filings
news.summary: RTW Investments reported a beneficial stake of roughly 3.94M shares (about 5.7%) and Susquehanna-affiliated entities disclosed a 3.34M-share (4.8%) position in filings accepted by the SEC on August 14. The disclosures point to continued institutional accumulation ahead of the September AMT-130 four-year data and the Q3 BLA submission.

news.headline: Stifel reiterates Buy on uniQure with a $71 price target into the September readout
news.summary: Stifel maintained its Buy rating and $71 target, pointing to the cleared FDA accelerated-approval pathway for AMT-130 and the four-year Phase I/II data as the next major stock catalyst. Sell-side consensus now sits near a $70 average target with no sell ratings across roughly 12-22 covering analysts.

news.headline: uniQure says an FDA advisory committee for AMT-130 is likely and welcomes the scrutiny
news.summary: Chief Medical Officer Walid Abi-Saab said the company considers an advisory committee meeting for its Huntington's gene therapy probable and is preparing for one, even though the FDA has not formally requested it. His comments came as regulatory uncertainty over unpredictable FDA advisory practices spread across biopharma.

news.headline: Wolfe Research upgrades uniQure to Outperform, sees a clear path to approval for AMT-130
news.summary: Wolfe moved to Outperform with a $65 target, arguing the market prices AMT-130 approval odds below 50% while Wolfe models roughly 70%, with peak U.S. sales potential near $2 billion. The upgrade followed the FDA's June agreement to accept three-year data as the primary basis for an accelerated-approval BLA.

news.headline: uniQure reports Q2 2026 results, confirms Q3 BLA timeline and cash runway into 2030
news.summary: Revenue was $5.8M and cash plus investments stood at $810.3M as of June 30 after the $259M June raise, funding operations into 2030, while the net loss widened to $81.1M on commercial-readiness spending. Management said final FDA meeting minutes received in July confirmed the accelerated-approval alignment, kept the AMT-130 BLA and UK MAA on track for Q3 2026 with a priority review request, guided to four-year Phase I/II data in September from a June 30 data cut, and detailed the confirmatory study design (randomized standard-of-care control, Total Functional Capacity at 36 months).

catalysts.label: Four-year AMT-130 data readout
catalysts.detail: uniQure plans to report four-year topline safety and efficacy data on all 24 patients from the first two Phase I/II cohorts (12 high-dose, 12 low-dose), plus three-year follow-up on three additional high-dose patients, from a June 30, 2026 data cut. The comparison uses an updated Enroll-HD natural-history database of roughly 26,000 participants. The company has said it is in a self-imposed quiet period until this readout, which as of September 2 had not yet been announced; it is the single biggest near-term catalyst for the stock, landing just ahead of the BLA filing and any advisory committee decision.

catalysts.label: AMT-130 US BLA submission
catalysts.detail: uniQure remains on track to submit the BLA for AMT-130 in Huntington's disease under the FDA accelerated-approval pathway in Q3 2026, a window that closes September 30. It intends to request priority review on the back of its RMAT and Breakthrough Therapy designations, based on final June/July meeting minutes confirming the three-year analysis can serve as the primary clinical basis. As of September 2 the filing had not yet been confirmed as submitted.

catalysts.label: UK MHRA marketing authorization application
catalysts.detail: Following a successful MHRA pre-submission meeting, uniQure plans a parallel UK MAA for AMT-130 in Q3 2026 on the same three-year data package. That gives a second potential approval route independent of the FDA and a first-mover position in a market where no disease-modifying Huntington's therapy exists.

catalysts.label: ICER scoping comment deadline
catalysts.detail: ICER's public comment period on the draft scoping document for its AMT-130 review closes September 11, 2026, with a revised scoping document to follow. The framing set here shapes the value benchmark US payers will use against uniQure's eventual price.

catalysts.label: FDA advisory committee (AdCom) meeting
catalysts.detail: Management believes an advisory committee review is likely for what would be the first gene therapy for Huntington's disease and says it is preparing for one. The FDA has not confirmed a meeting or a date, and timing would follow BLA acceptance rather than submission.

catalysts.label: Confirmatory trial design finalized and initiated
catalysts.detail: The FDA requires a randomized, concurrent standard-of-care-controlled confirmatory study with Total Functional Capacity at 36 months as the primary endpoint. uniQure says it intends to start this global trial as soon as possible after the BLA submission, and the design must be agreed with the agency before filing.

catalysts.label: Additional international regulatory pathways
catalysts.detail: uniQure said it is actively pursuing further registration routes for AMT-130 beyond the US and UK, including EU options, and expects to give an update in the second half of 2026. Any added jurisdiction expands the addressable launch footprint beyond the roughly 30,000 US patients.

catalysts.label: Q3 2026 results and BLA acceptance update
catalysts.detail: uniQure's Q3 2026 print is expected around November 9-10, 2026, per consensus earnings-calendar estimates (not yet formally confirmed by the company). It is the first scheduled opportunity for management to confirm that the BLA was filed and accepted, whether priority review was granted, and what PDUFA date applies, and to update commercial build-out spending against the roughly $810M cash position.

catalysts.label: AMT-260 higher-dose epilepsy data and AMT-191 Fabry update
catalysts.detail: uniQure plans updated Phase I/IIa data in refractory mesial temporal lobe epilepsy in H1 2027, including the second, higher-dose cohort (3x10^12 gc/mL) that completed enrollment around mid-2026. First-cohort data showed 79-100% disabling-seizure reductions in three of six patients and mixed results in the other three; a Fabry (AMT-191) update is guided to the same window.

catalysts.label: Potential accelerated approval decision and ICER verdict
catalysts.detail: If the BLA is accepted with priority review, an FDA decision on the first potential Huntington's gene therapy could land around mid-2027. ICER's draft evidence report is due January 19, 2027, with a Midwest CEPAC public meeting March 25 and the final report April 29, 2027, framing the US pricing debate for a therapy expected to be priced in line with other one-time gene therapies.

pulse: QURE trades in the high-$40s (roughly $47-51 depending on the session) for a market cap around $3.2-3.5B, up sharply over the past year but off its $71.50 52-week high, with the whole valuation resting on AMT-130. The regulatory setup improved sharply through June and July - the FDA reversed course and accepted three-year Phase I/II data as the primary basis for an accelerated-approval BLA, final meeting minutes confirmed it, Roche's exit from Huntington's removed the last late-stage competitor, and the Q2 print locked in $810M of cash and runway into 2030. August was newsflow-quiet on the operational side (RTW/Susquehanna institutional stake disclosures and ICER opening its formal cost-effectiveness review were the main items), consistent with management's self-imposed quiet period ahead of the September four-year AMT-130 data; as of September 2 that readout and the Q3 US BLA/UK MAA filings had not yet been announced, leaving an unconfirmed FDA advisory-committee meeting and the ICER pricing verdict as the two main open risks sitting just behind them.
